baseball: compact sports field with a clear baseball diamond layout and surrounding open play area, distinguishing baseball from stadium by lacking a large enclosed spectator structure, from field by having a more regular sports-specific geometric pattern, and from meadow by lacking broad natural grassland texture.
beach: bright shoreline region with clear sand-water boundary and open coastal texture, distinguishing beach from desert by direct water contact, from river by coastal shoreline appearance rather than a continuous inland channel, and from harbor by lacking strong dock-side port infrastructure.
bridge: narrow man-made crossing structure spanning water or land, distinguishing bridge from river by being a crossing rather than a watercourse, from harbor by lacking strong dock-side port context, and from overpass by emphasizing crossing over water or terrain rather than elevated road-over-road transport structure.
dense_residential: tightly packed residential roofs with very high housing density and minimal spacing, distinguishing dense_residential from sparse_residential by much smaller spacing, from meadow by lacking open vegetation texture, and from intersection by roof-dominant neighborhood structure rather than compact road-node geometry.
desert: broad barren region with dry homogeneous texture and very little vegetation, distinguishing desert from beach by lacking a clear shoreline water boundary, from field by lacking organized cultivated surface patterns, and from meadow by drier and more barren surface texture.
field: broad open land surface with relatively uniform texture, distinguishing field from meadow by more organized land appearance, from baseball by lacking sports-specific geometry, and from dense_residential by lacking dense roof clusters.
forest: dense continuous tree canopy with dark green natural texture, distinguishing forest from meadow by stronger canopy continuity, from field by lacking organized open-land structure, and from river by vegetation-dominant appearance rather than a continuous water channel.
harbor: waterfront maritime area with docks, vessels, and shore-adjacent port infrastructure, distinguishing harbor from bridge by lacking a simple narrow crossing structure, from river by stronger dock-water logistics organization, and from storage_tank by clearer shoreline maritime context.
intersection: road junction where multiple transportation lines meet, distinguishing intersection from overpass by weaker elevated overlap structure, from parking by lacking organized parked-vehicle row layout, and from dense_residential by compact road-node geometry rather than roof-dominant neighborhood texture.
meadow: broad natural grass-covered open area with soft vegetation texture and weak structural boundaries, distinguishing meadow from forest by lacking dense continuous canopy, from field by weaker man-made organization, and from sparse_residential by lacking repeated roof structures.
overpass: elevated crossing transport structure with visible grade separation, distinguishing overpass from bridge by emphasizing road-over-road transport structure, from intersection by stronger elevated overlap pattern, and from railway by lacking parallel rail-line texture.
parking: large open paved area with organized parking rows and vehicle-oriented layout, distinguishing parking from harbor by lacking strong dock-water context, from intersection by stronger row-like parking organization instead of crossing-road geometry, and from stadium by lacking a central sports-field structure.
railway: elongated rail corridor with parallel tracks and linear transport structure, distinguishing railway from overpass by stronger track-line continuity, from river by rail-line texture rather than a water channel, and from parking by lacking vehicle-row organization.
river: elongated natural watercourse with continuous winding channel and visible banks, distinguishing river from bridge by being a water body rather than a crossing, from harbor by weaker dock-side infrastructure, and from meadow by stronger water-channel continuity.
sparse_residential: widely separated residential houses with large open gaps and low housing density, distinguishing sparse_residential from dense_residential by much larger spacing, from meadow by repeated roof structures instead of open vegetation texture, and from field by clearer neighborhood housing layout.
stadium: large sports complex with prominent field and stronger enclosure or spectator-related structure, distinguishing stadium from baseball by larger scale and stronger venue framing, from parking by lacking organized parked-vehicle rows as the dominant structure, and from storage_tank by lacking compact circular industrial containers.
storage_tank: clusters of large circular industrial tanks with highly regular round geometry, distinguishing storage_tank from harbor by weaker shoreline maritime context, from stadium by compact circular industrial units instead of a sports venue, and from railway by lacking elongated parallel track structure.
